# Smartphone Laser-Scatter Turbidity Meter: Project Explanation

*This file is generated by `steps/make_report.py` from the saved results. Edit
`docs/explanation_template.md`, not `explanation.md`. All numbers below come from the code outputs.*

---

## 0. The one-minute version

**Problem.** Estimate water turbidity (NTU) cheaply, using a phone camera and a red laser instead of a
dedicated turbidimeter.

**Idea.** Shine a red laser through the water sample and photograph it straight down the beam in RAW.
Particles scatter light out of the beam, so the more turbid the water, the more the laser spot's light
**spreads out**. We measure that spread from the image and calibrate it against known NTU standards.

**What we built:**
- A complete Python pipeline: RAW DNG → physics-based feature → NTU.
- A command-line tool (`predict.py`) and a web app (`streamlit run src/app.py`).
- Automatic quality checks, a frozen and versioned model, and a full analysis trail (one script per step).

**Headline results (honest):**

| | |
|---|---|
| Data | 30 RAW images = **6 independent samples** (0, 10, 50, 200, 400, 800 NTU) × 5 burst shots |
| Signal used | `decay_len_inner`: how fast the laser light fades with distance from the centre |
| Final model | log-log >=200 + floor: log10(NTU) = -7.97 + 2.15 · ln(decay_len_inner / px), valid for decay_len_inner ≥ 113.1 px |
| Quantifiable range | **200–800 NTU**. Below ~156 NTU → "below range" (no number given) |
| Held-out accuracy | MAE 49 NTU, R² 0.94. Held-out means: 200 → 217, 400 → 358, 800 → 882 NTU |
| Classification | 100 % of 0–50 NTU images correctly "below range"; 14/15 images at 200–800 correctly quantified |
| Uncertainty quoted | ×/÷ 2.41 (1 sd, includes the one miss). Typical error when classified correctly: ×/÷ 1.23 |
| Main limitation | **Mechanical stability of the setup**, not camera noise. The spot moved up to 86 px within a burst |
| Status | Working proof of concept. Next step is a proper calibration run (Section 10) |

---

## 1. Problem statement and physics

**What turbidity is.** Turbidity is the cloudiness of water caused by suspended particles. It is reported
in NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Units) and calibrated against formazin standards. Standard instruments
(EPA 180.1, ISO 7027) measure light scattered at **90°** to the beam. Our setup does not do that, so it is
an **alternative optical method calibrated to NTU**, not a standards-compliant nephelometer.

**Our measurement principle: forward-scatter spread.**
- A collimated laser crossing clean water stays a tight beam.
- Particles scatter part of the light into small forward angles, so the beam arrives at the camera with
  a wider halo around it.
- More particles means more light pushed from the core into the halo: the intensity profile falls off
  **more slowly** with radius.
- So we measure the **decay length**: the radius over which the light in the flank of the spot drops by a
  factor of e (≈ 2.7). A longer decay length means more turbid water.

**Why RAW and not JPEG.** JPEG applies tone curves, sharpening, noise reduction and multi-frame fusion,
all of which change blur and brightness. A Bayer RAW DNG gives the **linear photon counts** from a single
exposure. We verified it really is a single raw frame: lag-1 noise autocorrelation is 0.06 (fused or
denoised images show much higher values).

## 2. Experimental setup

*Table – Acquisition setup* (`outputs/tables/setup.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/setup.png`)

| Item | Setting | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Camera | iPhone 16, main (wide) lens, 26 mm equiv. | iPhone 16 back camera 5.96mm f/1.6 |
| Capture app / format | Lightroom iOS, DNG | raw_type=Flat (Bayer, not ProRAW) |
| Sensor data | 12-bit, CFA BGGR | black 528, white 4095 DN |
| ISO / shutter / aperture | 40 / 1/2000 s / f/1.6 | identical on all 30 |
| Focus / white balance | manual 25 %, fixed WB | set in app |
| Image size | 4032×3024 px (planes 2016×1512) |  |
| Light source | red laser + dot-generator cap | wavelength not measured |
| Geometry | camera looks straight down the beam through the cuvette | dark box |

**Why these settings:**
- ISO 40 (the lowest) and 1/2000 s keep noise and motion low.
- Fixed focus and white balance stop the phone re-tuning itself between shots.
- The dark box removes ambient light.

**Weakness found later:** even at 1/2000 s the image is heavily saturated (Section 4). A shorter
exposure or an ND filter is the first hardware fix.

- cross-validation that holds out a whole sample.

## 4. Pipeline: what each step does and why

```
DNG (Bayer RAW)
  └─► split into colour planes R, G1, G2, B (no demosaic, no white balance → stays linear)
      └─► pick the B plane (least clipped; the red laser leaks weakly into blue pixels)
          └─► find spot centre (intensity-weighted centroid of the smoothed plane)
              └─► crop a fixed 1200×1200 px region around it
                  └─► mask saturated pixels (≥ white level − 64 DN)
                      └─► radial profile: average brightness in 5-px rings
                          └─► decay length = −1 / slope of ln(brightness) vs radius, r = 300–450 px
                              └─► model → NTU (or "below range") + quality flags
```

| Step | What we did | Why | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Inspect | Loaded all 30 DNGs, checked EXIF, bit depth, CFA, noise | Confirm genuine single-frame Bayer RAW with identical settings | `outputs/step1_*.png` |
| 2 Preprocess | Compared colour channels, found centre, chose crop, measured clipping | Find a channel and region where the data is trustworthy | `outputs/step2_roi.png`, `step2_clip_ratio.png` |
| 3 Radial profile | Brightness vs radius for every image, log scale | See how the shape changes with NTU | `outputs/step3_radial_profiles.png` |
| 4 Derivative features | Decay lengths, core/halo ratio, Tenengrad, Laplacian, FWHM … | Candidate blur/scatter measures | `outputs/step4_features.png` |
| 5 FFT features | Hann-windowed power spectrum: HF ratio, slope, cutoffs | The frequency-domain view of blur | `outputs/step5_fft.png` |
| 6 Feature selection | Spearman, error bars, separation, redundancy | Pick features that really carry information | `outputs/step6_feature_selection.png` |
| 7 Model | 5 models, leave-one-sample-out CV | Honest accuracy on unseen samples | `outputs/step7_model.png`, `models/` |
| 8 Robustness | Centre error, exposure, added noise | How fragile is the prediction? | `outputs/step8_robustness.png` |
| 9 Software | CLI, web app, QC, frozen model | Usable tool | `predict.py`, `src/app.py` |
| 10 Docs | README, protocol, limitations | Reproducibility | `README.md`, this file |

## 5. Findings, step by step

### 5.1 The sensor is heavily saturated, so we use the blue channel

*Table – Clipping per channel (raw DN ≥ 4095), mean of 5 shots* (`outputs/tables/saturation.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/saturation.png`)

| NTU | R clipped, frame (%) | G1 clipped, frame (%) | G2 clipped, frame (%) | B clipped, frame (%) | B clipped, ROI (%) | B near-clip (%) | B saturated out to r (px) | flagged (B ROI > 1 %) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 10.02 | 1.96 | 1.21 | 0.16 | 0.35 | 4.26 | 326 | 0/5 |
| 10 | 10.66 | 2.44 | 1.51 | 0.8 | 1.7 | 4.53 | 331 | 5/5 |
| 50 | 10.14 | 2.29 | 1.47 | 0.64 | 1.35 | 4.25 | 324 | 5/5 |
| 200 | 8.94 | 1.83 | 1.31 | 0.14 | 0.3 | 0.97 | 256 | 0/5 |
| 400 | 10.49 | 1.89 | 1.43 | 0.06 | 0.12 | 0.36 | 245 | 0/5 |
| 800 | 9.54 | 1.02 | 1.06 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 192 | 0/5 |

- **R is unusable** at the centre: about a quarter of red pixels in the crop are clipped at every NTU.
- Red light leaks into the other filters at a fixed small fraction (table below), so the **B channel
  acts as a built-in ~14× neutral-density filter**.
- Even B is saturated near the centre for 0–50 NTU, so all measurements are taken **outside r = 300 px**.

*Table – Channel sensitivity to the red laser (median per-pixel ratio, R in 0.2–0.9)* (`outputs/tables/ratios.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/ratios.png`)

| NTU | G1/R | G2/R | B/R | G1/G2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.1834 ± 0.0001 | 0.1847 ± 0.0001 | 0.0712 ± 0.0001 | 0.9925 ± 0.0004 |
| 10 | 0.1851 ± 0.0003 | 0.1860 ± 0.0004 | 0.0718 ± 0.0002 | 0.9940 ± 0.0008 |
| 50 | 0.1815 ± 0.0002 | 0.1827 ± 0.0002 | 0.0710 ± 0.0002 | 0.9912 ± 0.0011 |
| 200 | 0.1840 ± 0.0002 | 0.1850 ± 0.0003 | 0.0710 ± 0.0001 | 0.9934 ± 0.0006 |
| 400 | 0.1840 ± 0.0001 | 0.1846 ± 0.0001 | 0.0709 ± 0.0000 | 0.9962 ± 0.0007 |
| 800 | 0.1829 ± 0.0006 | 0.1834 ± 0.0008 | 0.0702 ± 0.0005 | 0.9957 ± 0.0014 |

The ratios are identical across NTU (B/R ≈ 0.071, G/R ≈ 0.184), so the leak is a fixed
property of the camera and not of the water. They do vary with position in the frame (≈ 0.13 → 0.05 from
r = 425 to 800 px), but identically for every sample, so the calibration absorbs it.

### 5.3 Radial profile: the turbidity signal is visible

*Table – B-channel radial profile (normalised intensity, 1 = clip), mean of 5 shots* (`outputs/tables/profile.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/profile.png`)

| NTU | first unclipped r (px) | I(200) | I(300) | I(400) | I(500) | I(590) | I(300)/I(500) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 278 | clipped | 0.457 | 0.183 | 0.076 | 0.037 | 6.04 ± 0.03 |
| 10 | 280 | clipped | 0.445 | 0.166 | 0.066 | 0.032 | 6.80 ± 0.29 |
| 50 | 278 | clipped | 0.452 | 0.181 | 0.074 | 0.036 | 6.09 ± 0.02 |
| 200 | 196 | 0.553 | 0.269 | 0.116 | 0.053 | 0.029 | 5.03 ± 0.14 |
| 400 | 170 | 0.499 | 0.264 | 0.126 | 0.061 | 0.034 | 4.31 ± 0.18 |
| 800 | 6 | 0.345 | 0.201 | 0.107 | 0.057 | 0.034 | 3.51 ± 0.05 |

- On a log scale the flank is nearly a straight line, i.e. an exponential fall-off.
- The fall-off gets **shallower with turbidity**: I(300)/I(500) drops 6.0 → 5.0 → 4.3 → 3.5 from 50 to
  800 NTU.
- **0, 10 and 50 NTU are indistinguishable.** At low turbidity almost all light is unscattered, and the
  image is just the camera's own out-of-focus disc.

| feature | 0 NTU | 10 NTU | 50 NTU | 200 NTU | 400 NTU | 800 NTU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decay length, flank (px) | 108.9 ± 0.3 | 101.5 ± 2.6 | 108.5 ± 0.3 | 120.6 ± 2.0 | 134.7 ± 4.4 | 157.6 ± 1.5 |
| decay length, halo (px) | 123.9 ± 0.3 | 120.0 ± 2.1 | 122.4 ± 0.4 | 140.5 ± 1.6 | 147.8 ± 4.4 | 167.6 ± 1.2 |

| Tenengrad (norm.) | 0.0599 ± 0.0006 | 0.0652 ± 0.0020 | 0.0618 ± 0.0039 | 0.0485 ± 0.0027 | 0.0387 ± 0.0014 | 0.0336 ± 0.0056 |
| Laplacian var (norm.) | 4.72e-04 ± 8.81e-06 | 5.05e-04 ± 1.27e-05 | 4.92e-04 ± 3.95e-05 | 3.87e-04 ± 2.42e-05 | 3.11e-04 ± 7.30e-06 | 2.80e-04 ± 5.19e-05 |
| spectral slope | -6.01 ± 0.04 | -5.64 ± 0.05 | -6.03 ± 0.08 | -6.35 ± 0.17 | -7.21 ± 0.20 | -7.85 ± 0.39 |
| HF ratio (as-is) | 3.56e-03 ± 7.69e-05 | 4.48e-03 ± 1.97e-04 | 3.57e-03 ± 1.17e-04 | 4.41e-04 ± 1.73e-04 | 1.11e-04 ± 3.63e-05 | 5.10e-05 ± 8.71e-06 |
| FWHM (px) | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | 479 ± 11 |

- FWHM (and the other peak-based widths) exists only for 800 NTU, because every other sample has a
  clipped peak.
- The **as-is HF ratio** looked excellent at first, but it was really measuring the edge of the clipped
  plateau. The trend disappears when all images are clipped at the same level.
- In the FFT, all real signal sits below ~0.008 cycles/px (periods > 125 px). Above that is pure sensor
  noise, so FFT features only re-encode the radial profile.

- **Every trustworthy feature correlates at |r| ≥ 0.95 with every other.** They all measure the same
  physical thing: how far the light spreads.
- Using 4 features would add **no information**, only more freedom to overfit 6 points.
- We chose **`decay_len_inner`**. It has the best worst-case separation between neighbouring levels
  (50 → 200 → 400 → 800), 1 % shot-to-shot variation, and it is a fit over 150 px of valid data, so it is
  robust.
- Spectral slope and Tenengrad are kept as independent cross-checks.

## 6. Model and accuracy

**Validation design.** Leave-one-sample-out (LOGO) cross-validation: train on 5 samples, predict the 6th,
repeat 6 times. Each fold hides a whole NTU level, so predicting 0 or 800 NTU is pure extrapolation. This
is the honest way to estimate performance on a new water sample. We always compare against a
**null model** (predict the training mean).

*Table – Leave-one-sample-out CV (6 folds; each fold holds out a whole NTU level)* (`outputs/tables/models.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/models.png`)

| model | MAE (NTU) | RMSE (NTU) | R² | RMSE log10(NTU+1) | chosen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| null (train mean) | 248 | 357 | -0.57 | 1.19 |  |
| log-log, 1 feature | 783 | 1756 | -36.95 | 0.86 |  |
| log-log >=200 + floor | 49 | 67 | 0.94 | 0.79 | ✔ |
| ridge, 2 features | 497 | 1059 | -12.81 | 0.83 |  |
| GBM, 2 features | 147 | 206 | 0.48 | 1.11 |  |

*Table – Mean held-out prediction per level (NTU)* (`outputs/tables/per_level.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/per_level.png`)

| model | true 0 | true 10 | true 50 | true 200 | true 400 | true 800 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| null (train mean) | 128 | 79 | 58 | 44 | 38 | 33 |
| log-log, 1 feature | 42 | 5 | 10 | 45 | 183 | 5041 |
| log-log >=200 + floor | below range | below range | below range | 217 | 358 | 882 |
| ridge, 2 features | 41 | 4 | 10 | 51 | 196 | 3342 |
| GBM, 2 features | 50 | 47 | 0 | 297 | 278 | 355 |

**Why the final model looks the way it does:**
- Fitting all 6 levels with one line fails badly: the flat 0–50 NTU cluster forces a steep slope, and
  800 NTU is extrapolated to 3000–5000.
- Ridge has the same problem. The GBM (tree model) cannot extrapolate at all.
- The chosen model fits a log-log line on the **quantifiable levels (200–800)**. It classifies anything
  below a learned threshold as **"below range"** and does not invent a number for it.

**Final equation:** log10(NTU) = -7.97 + 2.15 · ln(decay_len_inner / px), valid for decay_len_inner ≥ 113.1 px

| APC_0213.dng | 200 | 217 | 264 | +32 % | yes |
| APC_0214.dng | 200 | 185 | below range | – | NO |
| APC_0216.dng | 800 | 839 | 917 | +15 % | yes |
| APC_0217.dng | 800 | 837 | 914 | +14 % | yes |
| APC_0218.dng | 800 | 837 | 914 | +14 % | yes |
| APC_0219.dng | 800 | 775 | 842 | +5 % | yes |
| APC_0220.dng | 800 | 760 | 824 | +3 % | yes |

**The one miss (APC_0214)** is the 200 NTU shot taken right after the spot jumped 30 px. In the same way,
the two 400 NTU shots taken *before* the 400 NTU jump read ~300 NTU, and the three after it read ~400. **The errors follow
the geometry changes, not the turbidity.**

**What the error numbers mean:**
- MAE 49 NTU and R² 0.94 are computed on held-out samples, but they rest on **only 3
  quantifiable levels**. They show the method works; they are **not** a validated instrument accuracy.
- The reported uncertainty is ×/÷ 2.41 (1 sd). It includes the geometry miss, so it is
  deliberately conservative.
- Why the floor is ~156 NTU and not 50: there is **no data between 50 and 200 NTU**, so the
  learned threshold falls in that gap. More levels there will move it.

## 7. Robustness

*Table – Robustness: change in predicted NTU (one shot per sample)* (`outputs/tables/robustness.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/robustness.png`)

| test | level | median abs Δpred % (≥200 NTU) | worst abs Δpred % | fit band intact (worst) | floor-class flips |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exposure | 0.5 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 100 % | 0 |
| exposure | 0.7 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 100 % | 0 |
| exposure | 1.4 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 90 % | 0 |
| exposure | 2.0 | 0.7 | 0.9 | 60 % | 0 |
| noise | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0.1 | 100 % | 0 |
| noise | 2.0 | 0.0 | 0.1 | 100 % | 0 |
| noise | 4.0 | 0.0 | 0.3 | 100 % | 0 |
| shift | 5.0 | 1.3 | 2.4 | 100 % | 0 |
| shift | 10.0 | 2.9 | 4.7 | 100 % | 0 |
| shift | 20.0 | 4.7 | 10.3 | 100 % | 0 |
| shift | 40.0 | 11.4 | 23.5 | 97 % | 0 |
| shift | 80.0 | 23.9 | 57.4 | 73 % | 6 |

| Perturbation | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Camera noise (1–4× the sensor's own noise model) | Negligible (≤ 0.3 %) |
| Exposure ×0.5–1.4 (simulated) | No change, but this is guaranteed mathematically (a log-slope ignores scaling). A real exposure bracket is still needed |
| Exposure ×2 | 200–800 NTU fine. At 0–50 NTU the fit region clips → the QC **rejects** the image instead of giving a wrong answer |
| Centre error | 10 px → ~5 %, 20 px → ~10 %, 40 px → ~24 %, 80 px → ~57 %. Strongly direction-dependent |

**Conclusion:** the algorithm is robust to noise and exposure. It is sensitive to **geometry**, which is
exactly what went wrong during data collection. The fix is mechanical (a rigid mount), not algorithmic.

## 8. Software deliverables

| Deliverable | What it does | How to run |
|---|---|---|
| `predict.py` | CLI, one or many DNGs → NTU or "below range" + QC | `.venv/bin/python predict.py IMG.dng [--json]` |
| `src/app.py` | Web app: upload DNG, see spot, crop, profile vs calibration, result | `.venv/bin/streamlit run src/app.py` |
| `src/pipeline.py` | The single feature path used by training, tests, CLI and app | – |
| `src/service.py` | `analyse()`: features + model + QC verdict | – |
| `models/turbidity_model.joblib` | Trained model + metadata (feature range, floor, error, calibration EXIF) | – |
| `models/params.json` | Frozen preprocessing parameters. The model refuses to load if code differs | – |
| `steps/step1…8_*.py` | Full, reproducible analysis, one script per step | `for s in steps/step*.py; do .venv/bin/python $s; done` |
| `steps/make_report.py` | Regenerates all tables (CSV/MD/PNG) and this document | `.venv/bin/python steps/make_report.py` |

**Quality checks built into every prediction:**

| Check | Trigger | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Spot not found | Nothing stands out above background | **Rejected**, no number |
| Fit region saturated | Any ring in r = 300–450 px clipped | **Rejected**: "shorten exposure" |
| Crop off the frame | > 1 % of crop outside the image | **Rejected** |
| Spot near edge | Centre < 450 px from the frame edge | Warning |
| Different camera settings | ISO / shutter / aperture / lens ≠ calibration | Warning |
| Outside calibration | Feature beyond the trained range | Warning: "extrapolating" |
| Below range | Prediction below ~156 NTU | Reports "below range" + an upper bound, **no number** |

**Engineering choices worth mentioning:**
- **One code path.** Training asserts the pipeline reproduces the analysis features (difference ~1e-14),
  so the app can never compute something different from what was validated.
- **Frozen parameters.** Changing any preprocessing number without retraining stops the model from
  loading.
- **Pinned dependencies** (`requirements.txt`), and the data directory is configurable through
  `TURBIDITY_DATA_DIR`.

*Table – Frozen preprocessing parameters (models/params.json)* (`outputs/tables/params.csv`, slide image `outputs/tables/png/params.png`)

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| version | 1 |
| channel | B |
| centroid | {"sigma": 10, "frac": 0.5, "floor_pct": 5} |
| half | 600 |
| r_full | 595 |

## 9. Limitations (state these before anyone asks)

| Limitation | Evidence | Impact | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Only 6 independent samples | One cuvette per level; shots are bursts | All metrics optimistic; no between-fill variability measured | ≥ 3 separate fills per level |
| No data between 50 and 200 NTU | Calibration levels 0, 10, 50, 200, 400, 800 | Floor sits at ~156 NTU, an artefact of the gap | Add 75, 100, 150 NTU, … |
| 0–50 NTU unresolved | All features flat or misordered there | Can't serve drinking-water range (< 5 NTU) as built | Shorter exposure, longer path / different geometry |
| Setup moved during bursts | Spot jumps of 12–86 px | Dominant error (the one miss, 400 NTU split) | Rigid mount with cuvette stop |
| Heavy sensor saturation | R ~25 % clipped; B clipped to r ≈ 280 px at low NTU | Peak features unusable | Shorter shutter / ND filter |
| Geometry-specific calibration | Decay length is in pixels | New phone, focus, cuvette or distance = recalibrate | Calibration protocol below |
| Model design saw the data | "≥200 + floor" chosen after seeing 0–50 was flat | CV slightly optimistic | Confirm on a fresh, independent dataset |
| Not tested | Coloured water, particle types, bubbles, temperature, condensation | Unknown | Planned tests |
| Not a standards method | Forward-scatter imaging, not 90° nephelometry | Results are "NTU-calibrated", not EPA 180.1 / ISO 7027 | Cross-check against a reference turbidimeter |

---

## 10. Next steps: calibration protocol

1. **Rigid geometry:** fix phone, laser and cuvette mechanically, with an indexing stop for the cuvette.
2. **Independent samples:** ≥ 3 separate fills per level from fresh dilutions, cuvette re-seated
   between shots, levels shot in random order.
3. **Formazin (or StablCal) standards**, verified the same day with a reference turbidimeter.
4. **More levels:** 0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 600, 800, 1000 NTU.
5. **Exposure:** shorten the shutter (1/4000–1/8000 s) or add an ND filter until B is unclipped at 0 NTU.
   Shoot an exposure bracket (×0.5 / ×1 / ×2) per level.
6. **Dark frame** (laser off) and **blank frame** (clean water) every session, to track drift.
7. **Retrain:** add the files to `labels.csv`, run steps 1–7, then `make_report.py`.

**What success would look like:**
- a held-out error of ×/÷ ~1.2 or better across 50–1000 NTU, on independent fills;
- a defined detection limit backed by data, not by a gap in the calibration.

---

## 11. Likely questions and answers

**Q: How accurate is it?**
On held-out samples at 200–800 NTU, the mean predictions were 217 / 358 /
882 NTU for 200 / 400 / 800 NTU. MAE was 49 NTU. That rests on 3 quantifiable levels and
6 samples in total, so it is a proof of concept, not a spec. We quote ×/÷ 2.41 as the 1-sd
uncertainty.

**Q: Why not just use more images, or deep learning?**
The 30 images are 6 independent samples, so more shots of the same cuvette add no information. The
features are all one physical measurement, and a deep model would memorise 6 points. A one-parameter
physical model is the right complexity for this data.

**Q: Why can't it measure low turbidity (drinking water, < 5 NTU)?**
Below ~50 NTU almost no light is scattered, and the image is dominated by the camera's own defocus blur.
Measuring that range needs a longer optical path, a side-scatter (90°) geometry, or unsaturated exposure.
That is a hardware change, not a software one.

**Q: How do you know it measures turbidity and not brightness?**
- The feature is a **log-slope**, which ignores overall brightness by construction.
- Absolute brightness was checked and does **not** follow NTU (10 and 50 NTU were brighter than 0).
- Features that turned out to track clipping or signal-to-noise were found and excluded (Section 5.5).

**Q: What about ambient light, colour or bubbles?**
- Ambient light: shot in a dark box, and a dark-frame check is in the protocol.
- Coloured or absorbing water and bubbles: **not tested yet.** Absorption should mainly dim the image,
  which the log-slope ignores, but this must be verified.

**Q: Is it compliant with EPA 180.1 / ISO 7027?**
No. Those standards specify 90° nephelometric detection. This is a forward-scatter imaging method
calibrated to formazin NTU. It would need validation against a reference instrument.

**Q: How robust is it in the field?**
- Noise: ≤ 0.3 % effect. Exposure changes within the unsaturated range: none.
- Misalignment is the risk: 20 px of centre error ≈ 10 % error.
- The QC rejects saturated or off-frame images rather than reporting a wrong number.

**Q: What does it cost?**
A phone the user already owns, a laser pointer with a dot cap, a cuvette and a dark box. The software is
open Python.

**Q: What would you do with another month?**
Run the calibration protocol (Section 10), build a rigid mount, test coloured and particle-type samples,
and compare against a reference turbidimeter.

   Expected: 800 NTU sample ≈ 839, 200 NTU sample ≈ 224, 0 NTU sample → "below the quantifiable range".

## 13. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| NTU | Nephelometric Turbidity Unit, calibrated with formazin suspensions |
| DNG / Bayer RAW | Raw sensor data. Each pixel sees one colour (here B-G-G-R pattern), linear in light |
| CFA plane | The sub-image of one colour filter (half resolution), used without demosaicing |
| Clipping / saturation | Pixel reached the sensor's maximum (4095), so its true brightness is unknown |
| Radial profile | Average brightness at each distance from the spot centre |
| Decay length | Distance over which the flank brightness falls by e (≈ 2.7×). Longer = more scattering |
| Spearman ρ | Rank correlation: does the feature go up and down consistently with NTU? |
| LOGO CV | Leave-one-group-out cross-validation. Each fold hides one whole sample |
| MAE / RMSE / R² | Mean absolute error / root-mean-square error / fraction of variance explained |
| ×/÷ factor | Multiplicative error band. ×/÷ 2 means "between half and double" |
| QC | Automatic quality checks that reject or flag unreliable images |
